note: Principles of Accounts round 1 (part A): nature of accounting, concepts and conventions, source documents and books of original entry, accounting equation and ledger, trial balance, correction of errors and suspense account, ethics and regulatory bodies, cash book and discounts, petty cash, bank reconciliation, final accounts of a sole trader, year-end adjustments, depreciation and disposal - with a trial-balance extract, a bank reconciliation case, a petty cash table, an accounting-equation case and a machine-disposal case as data passages.

passages.title: Balances of Ngozi Stores
passages.text:
The following balances were extracted from
the books of Ngozi Stores, a sole trader,
on 31 December 2025.

Item                          ₦
Opening stock           120,000
Purchases               850,000
Sales                 1,400,000
Returns inwards          20,000
Returns outwards         15,000
Carriage inwards         10,000
Carriage outwards        25,000
Wages and salaries      180,000
Rent                     60,000
Discount received        12,000

Closing stock was valued at ₦150,000.

Postage stamps          4,500

passages.title: Kemi's first month in business
passages.text:
Kemi started a provisions business on 1 May 2026 with ₦500,000 cash. During May the following took place:
1. She bought goods on credit from Dele for ₦120,000.
2. She bought a motor van for cash, ₦200,000.
3. She sold goods which had cost ₦60,000 for ₦90,000 cash.
4. She paid Dele ₦50,000 cash on account.
5. She took ₦20,000 cash from the business for her personal use.

passages.title: Machine bought by Delta Bakery
passages.text: Delta Bakery bought a dough-mixing machine on 1 January 2023 for ₦2,400,000. The machine was expected to last five years and to have a scrap value of ₦400,000 at the end of that time. The bakery's financial year ends on 31 December. On 1 January 2026 the machine was sold for ₦1,000,000 cash.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Using the balances of Ngozi Stores, the net purchases for the year were
questions.explanation: Net purchases = purchases 850,000 − returns outwards 15,000 + carriage inwards 10,000 = ₦845,000. Carriage inwards is part of the cost of bringing goods in.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: The net sales (turnover) of Ngozi Stores for the year were
questions.explanation: Net sales = sales 1,400,000 − returns inwards 20,000 = ₦1,380,000. Returns outwards relate to purchases, not sales.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: The cost of goods sold by Ngozi Stores during the year was
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold = opening stock 120,000 + net purchases 845,000 − closing stock 150,000 = ₦815,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: The gross profit of Ngozi Stores for the year was
questions.explanation: Gross profit = net sales 1,380,000 − cost of goods sold 815,000 = ₦565,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: The net profit of Ngozi Stores for the year was
questions.explanation: Net profit = gross profit 565,000 + discount received 12,000 − (carriage outwards 25,000 + wages 180,000 + rent 60,000) = 577,000 − 265,000 = ₦312,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: In the trading account of Ngozi Stores, the cost of goods available for sale was
questions.explanation: Goods available for sale = opening stock 120,000 + net purchases 845,000 = ₦965,000, before deducting closing stock.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The adjusted cash book balance of Bello Enterprises on 31 March 2026 was
questions.explanation: Only items (iii) to (vi) go into the cash book: 86,000 − 2,500 − 6,000 + 9,000 − 7,500 = ₦79,000. Unpresented and uncredited cheques are timing differences.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The balance shown by the bank statement of Bello Enterprises on 31 March 2026 was
questions.explanation: Start from the adjusted cash book balance of 79,000, add unpresented cheques 24,000 (the bank has not yet paid them) and deduct uncredited lodgements 15,000: ₦88,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which item in the Bello Enterprises comparison increases the balance in the cash book?
questions.A: the dividend paid directly into the account
questions.C: the cheque returned marked 'refer to drawer'
questions.D: the bank charges shown only on the statement
questions.explanation: A dividend received directly by the bank is money the business did not know it had; it is debited in the cash book and increases the balance. The others reduce it.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The total amount that should be credited in the cash book of Bello Enterprises to bring it up to date is
questions.explanation: Credits (payments out) are bank charges 2,500 + standing order 6,000 + dishonoured cheque 7,500 = ₦16,000. The dividend is a debit.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the Bello Enterprises case, the cheque returned marked 'refer to drawer' means that
questions.A: the bank had already paid the cheque twice
questions.B: the customer had cancelled the sale
questions.C: the cheque was lodged after the closing date of the statement
questions.D: the customer's account did not have enough money to meet the cheque
questions.explanation: 'Refer to drawer' is written on a dishonoured cheque: the drawer's bank refuses payment, usually because the account has insufficient funds.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: The total petty cash payments of Gateway College for April 2026 amounted to
questions.explanation: 4,500 + 7,200 + 9,800 + 6,300 + 3,700 = ₦31,500 was spent from the imprest during the month.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: The cash remaining with the petty cashier of Gateway College on 30 April 2026 was
questions.explanation: Cash in hand = imprest 50,000 − payments 31,500 = ₦18,500 before the float is restored.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: The amount the bursar must give the petty cashier of Gateway College on 1 May 2026 to restore the imprest is
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system the cashier is reimbursed exactly what was spent, ₦31,500, so that the float returns to ₦50,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: When the Gateway College imprest is restored on 1 May 2026, the entry in the main cash book is
questions.A: debit petty cash book, credit bank ₦50,000
questions.C: debit petty cash account, credit bank ₦31,500
questions.D: debit sundry expenses, credit petty cash ₦31,500
questions.explanation: Reimbursement transfers ₦31,500 from the bank (credit) to the petty cash (debit); the expenses themselves are posted from the analysis column totals.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Kemi's cash balance at the end of May 2026 was
questions.explanation: Cash = 500,000 − 200,000 (van) + 90,000 (sales) − 50,000 (paid Dele) − 20,000 (drawings) = ₦320,000. The credit purchase did not involve cash.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: At the end of May 2026 Kemi owed her creditor Dele
questions.explanation: Dele supplied goods worth 120,000 and was paid 50,000, leaving a creditor balance of ₦70,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The total assets of Kemi's business on 31 May 2026 amounted to

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Kemi's capital at the end of May 2026 was
questions.explanation: Closing capital = opening capital 500,000 + profit (90,000 − 60,000 = 30,000) − drawings 20,000 = ₦510,000. Check: assets 580,000 − creditors 70,000 = 510,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of Kemi's May transactions changed the total of her assets without changing her capital or liabilities?
questions.A: buying the motor van for cash
questions.B: buying goods on credit from Dele
questions.explanation: Paying cash for a van simply exchanges one asset for another: total assets, liabilities and capital are all unchanged. The other transactions change liabilities or capital.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Using the straight-line method, the annual depreciation on Delta Bakery's machine is
questions.explanation: Straight line: (cost 2,400,000 − scrap 400,000) ÷ 5 years = ₦400,000 each year.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: The net book value of Delta Bakery's machine on 31 December 2025 under the straight-line method was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: If Delta Bakery had used the reducing-balance method at 20% per annum, the depreciation charge for 2025 would have been

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Under the straight-line method, the sale of Delta Bakery's machine on 1 January 2026 resulted in a
questions.explanation: Net book value on the date of sale was 1,200,000; sale proceeds 1,000,000; the shortfall of ₦200,000 is a loss on disposal charged to the profit and loss account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: The scrap value of ₦400,000 in the Delta Bakery case is the
questions.A: amount the machine can be sold for at any time
questions.C: annual repair cost of the machine
questions.D: estimated value of the machine at the end of its useful life
questions.explanation: Scrap (residual) value is the estimated amount recoverable when the asset is retired; it is deducted from cost before spreading the depreciable amount.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Recording the daily transactions of a shop in the books in a systematic manner is best described as
questions.explanation: Bookkeeping is the routine recording of transactions; accounting goes further to classify, summarise, interpret and report them.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The Italian monk who first published a description of the double entry system in 1494 was
questions.explanation: Luca Pacioli described double entry bookkeeping in his 1494 work Summa de Arithmetica, and is regarded as the father of accounting.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A bank considering a loan application from Ade Motors would be most interested in the firm's
questions.explanation: Lenders use accounting information to judge whether a business generates enough cash to service interest and repay the principal.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is an internal user of accounting information?
questions.explanation: Managers work inside the entity and use accounting information for planning and control; the others are external users.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A company published its 2024 financial statements in 2026. The information failed the qualitative characteristic of
questions.explanation: Information loses its capacity to influence decisions when it arrives too late; timeliness is an enhancing characteristic of useful information.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Presenting this year's figures side by side with last year's figures in the same format mainly enhances
questions.explanation: Comparability allows users to identify trends over time and differences between entities.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The branch of accounting that gathers financial evidence for use in court cases and fraud investigations is
questions.explanation: Forensic accounting applies investigative and accounting skills to disputes and litigation.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Cost accounting is primarily concerned with
questions.A: assessing the tax payable by a company
questions.B: recording receipts and payments of government
questions.C: expressing an opinion on published accounts
questions.D: ascertaining and controlling the cost of products and services
questions.explanation: Cost accounting accumulates and analyses costs so that management can price products and control expenditure.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Management accounting differs from financial accounting in that management accounting
questions.A: is governed strictly by accounting standards
questions.C: produces reports mainly for internal decision making
questions.explanation: Management accounting reports are prepared for managers, are not bound by reporting standards and often look to the future (budgets, forecasts).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The person who examines the financial statements of a company and expresses an independent opinion on them is the
questions.explanation: An auditor independently examines the records and reports whether the statements give a true and fair view.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader who cannot tell whether he made a profit or a loss last year most probably
questions.explanation: One of the main objectives of bookkeeping is to enable the profit or loss of a period to be determined; without records this is impossible.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A major objective of keeping accounting records by a sole trader is to
questions.D: ascertain the profit or loss for a period
questions.explanation: Records make it possible to prepare a trading and profit and loss account and to know the financial position at any date.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The accounts of the federal, state and local governments are prepared mainly to show
questions.A: how public funds were received and spent
questions.C: the market value of government shares
questions.explanation: Government (public sector) accounting is concerned with stewardship and accountability for public money, not profit.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The branch of accounting concerned with the effect of an organisation's activities on the community and on nature is
questions.explanation: Social and environmental accounting reports on matters such as pollution, community projects and employee welfare.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Accounting is often called the language of business because it
questions.A: is written and read only by professional accountants
questions.B: is taught as a compulsory course in every business school
questions.C: uses the English language in every country of the world
questions.D: communicates the financial results of an entity to interested parties
questions.explanation: Through statements and reports, accounting communicates the performance and position of an entity to owners, lenders and others.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of useful accounting information?
questions.explanation: Useful information should be reliable (faithfully representing what it claims), relevant, comparable and understandable.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The main difference between bookkeeping and accounting is that accounting
questions.A: is done only by the owner of the business and never by clerks
questions.B: records transactions without using the double entry system
questions.C: interprets and reports the recorded information for decision making
questions.D: stops at the trial balance stage and never goes beyond it
questions.explanation: Bookkeeping ends at recording; accounting summarises, analyses and interprets the records so users can make decisions.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Mr Okon paid his daughter's school fees from the shop's cash and the payment was recorded as drawings. The concept applied is
questions.explanation: The entity concept treats the business as separate from its owner, so private payments from business cash are drawings, not expenses.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Fixed assets are recorded at cost less depreciation rather than at their forced-sale values because of the
questions.explanation: Going concern assumes the business will continue operating, so assets are not valued as if they were about to be sold off.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader makes a provision for doubtful debts before any debtor actually fails to pay. This illustrates the concept of
questions.explanation: Prudence (conservatism) requires anticipating possible losses but not possible gains.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Electricity consumed in December 2025 but paid for in January 2026 is charged in the accounts for 2025 because of the
questions.explanation: Under the accrual (matching) concept, expenses are recognised in the period in which they are incurred, not when cash is paid.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The skill and loyalty of a company's chief engineer do not appear in its balance sheet because of the
questions.explanation: Only items that can be expressed in monetary terms are recorded; staff quality cannot be objectively measured in naira.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A company that changes its depreciation method every year to suit its profit target violates the concept of
questions.explanation: Consistency requires the same treatment of similar items from period to period so that results are comparable.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A stapler costing ₦1,500 that will last five years is written off as an expense in the year of purchase. The convention applied is
questions.explanation: Materiality permits insignificant items to be treated in the simplest way, since capitalising and depreciating a stapler would not affect any decision.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Land bought in 2010 for ₦3 million and now worth ₦30 million is still shown in the books at ₦3 million under the
questions.explanation: The historical cost concept records assets at the actual amount paid for them, which is objective and verifiable.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Revenue is recognised when goods are delivered to a customer and not when the order is received. This is the
questions.explanation: Under the realisation concept revenue is recognised when it is earned, that is when ownership of goods passes to the buyer.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Preparing financial statements at regular intervals of twelve months is required by the
questions.explanation: The periodicity (accounting period) concept divides the life of a business into regular periods for reporting.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The principle that every transaction affects at least two accounts is the
questions.explanation: Dual aspect is the basis of double entry: every debit has a corresponding credit.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Recording assets at amounts supported by invoices and receipts rather than the owner's personal estimates reflects
questions.explanation: Objectivity requires accounting records to be based on verifiable evidence free from personal bias.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A vehicle acquired under a finance lease is shown as an asset in the lessee's balance sheet although legal title remains with the lessor. This applies
questions.explanation: Substance over form reports the economic reality (the lessee enjoys the risks and rewards of ownership) rather than the legal form.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A note to the accounts describing a pending court case against the company is required by the convention of
questions.explanation: Full disclosure requires all information that could influence users' decisions to be reported, including contingencies.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Valuing closing stock at the lower of cost and net realisable value is an application of
questions.explanation: Prudence ensures that anticipated losses on stock are recognised at once while unrealised gains are ignored.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Zeta Ltd recorded a ₦20 million sale in December 2025 although the goods were delivered to the customer in February 2026. The concept breached is
questions.explanation: Revenue should be recognised when it is earned (goods delivered, ownership passed), so the sale belongs to the 2026 period.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The assumption that the purchasing power of the naira remains stable over time underlies the
questions.explanation: Money measurement records transactions in monetary units and assumes the unit is a stable measure, ignoring inflation.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Charging depreciation over the useful life of an asset rather than writing off the whole cost when bought applies the
questions.explanation: Matching spreads the cost of the asset over the periods that benefit from its use so that expenses are matched with the revenue they help earn.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Accounting conventions are best described as
questions.A: laws passed by the National Assembly
questions.B: instructions from the owner of a business
questions.D: customs and practices generally accepted by accountants
questions.explanation: Conventions such as consistency, materiality and prudence are generally accepted practices that guide the application of concepts.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A sole trader used ₦300,000 of business cash to buy a private car and debited motor vehicles account. The concept violated is
questions.explanation: The car is for private use, so the payment is drawings; treating it as a business asset mixes the owner's affairs with the entity's.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: The document sent by a seller to a buyer showing the goods supplied, their quantities and prices is
questions.explanation: The invoice is the source document for credit sales (to the seller) and credit purchases (to the buyer).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: A seller issues a credit note to a customer when
questions.A: the customer pays the amount due before the agreed date
questions.B: goods ordered by the customer are delivered to his premises
questions.C: the customer's cheque is returned unpaid by the bank
questions.D: goods are returned by the customer or the customer was overcharged
questions.explanation: A credit note reduces the amount owed by the customer, for example for returns or an overcharge on the invoice.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: A seller who discovers that a customer was undercharged on an invoice corrects the error by sending a
questions.explanation: A debit note increases the amount the customer owes; a credit note would reduce it.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: Goods bought on credit for resale are first recorded in the
questions.explanation: The purchases day book (purchases journal) lists credit purchases of goods from copies of suppliers' invoices.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: The purchase of a delivery van on credit from Toyota Nigeria is recorded in the
questions.explanation: Credit purchases of fixed assets are not goods for resale, so they go through the journal proper (general journal).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: The returns outwards book is written up from
questions.explanation: When goods are returned to a supplier, the supplier sends a credit note; copies are the source for the returns outwards journal.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: The sales day book is written up from
questions.A: copies of invoices sent to customers
questions.explanation: Each credit sale is evidenced by the invoice sent to the customer; the sales journal lists these invoices.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: A trader bought goods with a list price of ₦80,000 subject to a trade discount of 10%. The amount entered in the purchases day book is
questions.explanation: Trade discount is deducted on the invoice; the net amount 80,000 − 8,000 = ₦72,000 is recorded. Trade discount never appears in the ledger.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: Trade discount is
questions.A: recorded in the discount column of the cash book
questions.B: credited to the discount received account
questions.C: not recorded in the ledger accounts at all
questions.D: debited to the discount allowed account
questions.explanation: Trade discount is simply deducted on the invoice to arrive at the price; only cash discounts are entered in the books.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: Which of the following is both a book of original entry and a ledger account?
questions.explanation: The cash book records cash and bank transactions as they occur (prime entry) and also serves as the cash and bank accounts.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: Opening entries, the correction of errors and the writing off of bad debts are recorded in the
questions.explanation: The general journal (journal proper) records transactions that do not fit into any of the special journals, with a narration.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: A receipt is a document that
questions.A: orders a bank to pay money
questions.explanation: A receipt is issued by the person receiving cash or cheque as evidence of payment.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: The document completed when cash and cheques are paid into a bank account is the
questions.explanation: The pay-in slip (teller) lists the cash and cheques lodged and is the source document for bank deposits.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: A petty cash voucher is used to
questions.A: record the reimbursement of the imprest
questions.B: record purchases of goods on credit
questions.C: list the analysis columns of the petty cash book
questions.D: support each payment made from petty cash
questions.explanation: Every petty cash payment should be supported by a voucher signed by the person receiving the money and authorised by an officer.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: The person who writes and signs a cheque is called the
questions.explanation: The drawer signs the cheque, the drawee is the bank instructed to pay and the payee is the person to be paid.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: The total of the sales day book at the end of the month is posted to the
questions.B: credit of the debtors control account
questions.explanation: Individual invoices are debited to the customers; the periodic total is credited to sales account in the general ledger.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: Each entry in the purchases day book is posted to the
questions.A: credit of the individual supplier's account
questions.B: debit of the individual supplier's account
questions.explanation: Each credit purchase increases what is owed to the supplier (credit the personal account); the total is debited to purchases account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: A statement of account received monthly from a supplier is used by the buyer to
questions.A: record the month's purchases in the purchases day book
questions.B: replace the individual invoices received during the month
questions.C: calculate the trade discount allowed on each invoice
questions.D: check the balance owed against the supplier's account in the purchases ledger
questions.explanation: The statement summarises invoices, credit notes and payments; the buyer agrees it with the supplier's ledger account before paying.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Source Documents and Books of Original Entry
questions.q: Goods returned by a customer are recorded in the
questions.explanation: Sales returns (returns inwards) are listed in the returns inwards journal from copies of credit notes issued.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A business has assets of ₦950,000 and liabilities of ₦320,000. Its capital is
questions.explanation: Capital = assets − liabilities = 950,000 − 320,000 = ₦630,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: If capital is ₦400,000 and liabilities are ₦150,000, total assets amount to
questions.explanation: Assets = capital + liabilities = 400,000 + 150,000 = ₦550,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which transaction increases both total assets and total liabilities?
questions.explanation: Goods bought on credit increase stock (an asset) and creditors (a liability) by the same amount.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which transaction leaves the total assets of a business unchanged?
questions.explanation: Cash goes up and debtors go down by the same amount: one asset replaces another and the total is unchanged.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: When the owner takes goods from the business for personal use, the effect on the accounting equation is that
questions.explanation: Drawings of stock reduce the asset (stock) and reduce the owner's capital.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Paying a creditor ₦50,000 by cheque
questions.explanation: Bank (asset) falls by 50,000 and creditors (liability) fall by 50,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The accounts of individual debtors and creditors are classified as
questions.explanation: Personal accounts are those of persons and organisations; real accounts are for assets and nominal accounts for expenses, losses, incomes and gains.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Rent account and wages account are examples of
questions.explanation: Expenses and incomes are recorded in nominal (impersonal) accounts which are closed to the profit and loss account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Motor vehicles account is classified as a
questions.explanation: Real accounts record tangible property such as buildings, machinery and vehicles.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The rule 'debit the receiver, credit the giver' applies to
questions.explanation: For personal accounts, the person who receives value is debited and the person who gives value is credited.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The double entry for cash sales of ₦25,000 is
questions.explanation: Cash comes in (debit cash account) and sales revenue is earned (credit sales account).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Goods previously bought on credit from Musa are returned to him. The entry is
questions.explanation: The return reduces what is owed to Musa (debit his account) and is recorded in returns outwards account (credit).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A debit balance on a customer's account in the sales ledger means that
questions.explanation: Debtors' accounts normally have debit balances representing amounts due from customers.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The credit balance on the capital account of a sole trader represents
questions.D: the amount the business owes its owner
questions.explanation: Under the entity concept the owner is treated as a creditor of the business for the capital invested plus accumulated profits.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following accounts normally has a credit balance?
questions.explanation: Discount received is an income and, like sales and capital, has a credit balance; the others are debit balances.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The purchase of office furniture by cheque is recorded by
questions.explanation: A fixed asset account is debited and the bank account credited; it is not a purchase of goods for resale.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: When the owner introduces additional capital of ₦200,000 in cash, the entry is
questions.explanation: Cash (asset) increases so cash is debited; the owner's claim increases so capital is credited.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In a business that keeps a sales ledger, a purchases ledger and a general ledger, the discount allowed account is found in the
questions.explanation: Nominal accounts such as discount allowed are kept in the general (nominal) ledger; personal accounts go in the sales and purchases ledgers.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader has stock ₦60,000, debtors ₦40,000, cash ₦25,000 and a van ₦300,000. He owes creditors ₦45,000 and has a bank overdraft of ₦20,000. His capital is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The main purpose of extracting a trial balance is to
questions.A: calculate the profit for the year
questions.B: detect all errors in the books
questions.C: list the assets and liabilities of the business
questions.D: test the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger
questions.explanation: A trial balance checks that total debits equal total credits; it does not reveal every kind of error.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following appears on the credit side of a trial balance?
questions.explanation: Returns outwards reduce purchases and have a credit balance; the other three are debit balances.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following appears on the debit side of a trial balance?
questions.explanation: Carriage inwards is an expense (debit balance); sales, capital and creditors are credit balances.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Closing stock does not normally appear in the trial balance because
questions.A: it is not regarded as an asset of the business at the year end
questions.B: it belongs to the customers who have already paid for it
questions.C: it is always equal to the opening stock of the following year
questions.D: it is valued by physical count after the ledger balances have been extracted
questions.explanation: The stock figure at the year end comes from a stocktaking, so it is brought into the books only when the final accounts are prepared.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The totals of a trial balance agree. Which of the following errors may still exist in the books?
questions.B: posting only the debit entry of a transaction
questions.C: adding up the sales day book wrongly
questions.D: entering ₦4,500 as ₦5,400 in one account only
questions.explanation: Errors of principle, omission, commission, original entry, compensating errors and complete reversal do not disturb the agreement of the trial balance.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The debit total of a trial balance is ₦1,254,000 and the credit total is ₦1,238,000. Pending discovery of the errors, the difference is
questions.D: written off to profit and loss, ₦16,000
questions.explanation: Debits exceed credits by 16,000, so a credit of ₦16,000 is entered in a suspense account to make the trial balance agree temporarily.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In a trial balance, the provision for doubtful debts appears as a
questions.explanation: A provision is a credit balance set against the debtors, which are a debit balance.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of these balances would appear on the same side of the trial balance as purchases?
questions.explanation: Purchases and drawings are both debit balances; the others are credit balances.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trial balance is usually extracted
questions.A: before any transaction of the period is posted to the ledger
questions.B: after the balance sheet of the period has been drawn up
questions.C: only when the business is about to be sold to a new owner
questions.D: at the end of an accounting period before the final accounts are prepared
questions.explanation: Balancing the ledger and listing the balances is the step between posting and preparing the final accounts.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Capital, sales, creditors and a loan from the bank are all
questions.explanation: Sources of funds (capital and liabilities) and incomes have credit balances.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Discount allowed of ₦4,000 was listed on the credit side of the trial balance instead of the debit side. The difference between the two totals is
questions.explanation: The debit side is short by 4,000 and the credit side is overstated by 4,000, giving a difference of ₦8,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Rent received of ₦30,000 appears in the trial balance of a trader as a
questions.explanation: Rent received is an income and therefore has a credit balance.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A bank overdraft is shown in the trial balance on the
questions.explanation: An overdraft is money owed to the bank; the bank column of the cash book has a credit balance.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The provision for depreciation on machinery appears in the trial balance as a
questions.explanation: The provision (accumulated depreciation) account collects the depreciation charged to date and is a credit balance deducted from the asset's cost.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: A credit sale of ₦45,000 to Bola was not recorded anywhere in the books. This is an error of
questions.explanation: An error of omission occurs when a transaction is completely left out of the books; the trial balance still agrees.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Cash paid to Chidi was correctly credited to cash but debited to the account of Chike, another supplier. This is an error of
questions.explanation: An error of commission posts the correct amount to the wrong account of the same class (a personal account for another personal account).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: The purchase of a computer for office use was debited to the purchases account. This is an error of
questions.explanation: An error of principle records a transaction in the wrong class of account, here capital expenditure treated as revenue expenditure.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: A sales invoice for ₦72,000 was entered in the sales day book as ₦27,000 and posted with that figure to both accounts. This is an error of
questions.explanation: When the wrong amount is entered in the book of original entry and carried through the double entry, it is an error of original entry.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: The sales day book was overcast by ₦10,000. The correcting entry is
questions.explanation: Sales account was over-credited by 10,000 while the individual debtors were correct, so sales is debited and suspense credited.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Cash received from a debtor was debited to the debtor's account and credited to cash account. This is an error of
questions.explanation: Both entries were made with the correct amount but on the wrong sides; the trial balance still agrees.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Purchases were undercast by ₦5,000 and, quite separately, sales were undercast by ₦5,000. These are
questions.explanation: Two independent errors of equal amount on opposite sides cancel each other out so the trial balance still agrees.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Which of the following errors would cause the trial balance to disagree?
questions.A: recording a sale to Ade in the account of Ada
questions.B: treating repairs as an addition to machinery
questions.C: posting only the debit side of a transaction
questions.explanation: A one-sided (single) entry means debits no longer equal credits; the other three errors keep the totals equal.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Discount allowed of ₦3,000 was credited to discount received account. The entry to correct the error is
questions.A: debit discount allowed ₦3,000, credit discount received ₦3,000
questions.D: debit discount allowed ₦3,000, debit discount received ₦3,000, credit suspense ₦6,000
questions.explanation: Discount allowed should have been debited 3,000; instead discount received was credited 3,000. Both must be corrected, and the 6,000 goes to suspense.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Returns outwards of ₦8,000 were correctly entered in the returns outwards account but not posted to the supplier's account. Before correction the suspense account would show
questions.explanation: The credit to returns outwards was made but the debit to the supplier was missing, so debits are short by 8,000 and suspense carries a debit of ₦8,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Wages of ₦25,000 paid to workers who installed a new machine were debited to wages account. As a result the net profit is
questions.explanation: Installation wages are part of the cost of the machine (capital expenditure); charging them as an expense reduces profit wrongly by ₦25,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: A suspense account was opened with a debit of ₦5,000. It was later found that the purchases account had been undercast by ₦5,000. The correcting entry is
questions.explanation: Purchases needs an extra debit of 5,000; the credit goes to suspense, which clears the balance.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Which of the following errors does not require the use of a suspense account for its correction?
questions.B: an addition error in a ledger account
questions.D: a balance omitted from the trial balance
questions.explanation: Errors of principle do not affect the agreement of the trial balance, so they are corrected by journal entries between the accounts concerned.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: After errors are corrected, the net profit previously reported must be adjusted when the error involved
questions.B: the cash and bank columns only
questions.explanation: Only errors touching nominal accounts (revenues and expenses) change the profit; errors between assets and liabilities affect the balance sheet only.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Goods worth ₦15,000 returned by a customer were recorded in the returns outwards book and posted accordingly. The correcting entry is
questions.A: debit returns inwards ₦15,000, credit returns outwards ₦15,000
questions.B: debit the customer ₦30,000, credit returns inwards ₦30,000
questions.C: debit returns inwards ₦15,000, debit returns outwards ₦15,000, credit the customer ₦30,000
questions.D: debit returns outwards ₦15,000, credit the customer ₦15,000
questions.explanation: The wrong entry debited the customer 15,000 and credited returns outwards; the correct entry needed a debit to returns inwards and a credit to the customer. Reversing and correcting gives a 30,000 credit to the customer.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Motor expenses of ₦12,000 were debited to motor vehicles account. The effect of the error is that
questions.A: profit is understated and assets are understated
questions.B: there is no effect on profit or assets
questions.C: profit is overstated and liabilities are understated
questions.D: profit is overstated and assets are overstated
questions.explanation: An expense was treated as an asset, so expenses are too low (profit too high) and fixed assets too high, each by ₦12,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: A trader's draft net profit was ₦480,000. It was then found that closing stock had been understated by ₦30,000 and that rent paid of ₦20,000 had been omitted. The corrected net profit is
questions.explanation: Higher closing stock raises profit by 30,000; the omitted rent reduces it by 20,000: 480,000 + 30,000 − 20,000 = ₦490,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Correction of Errors and Suspense Account
questions.q: Cash of ₦18,000 received from Femi, a debtor, was debited to Femi's account and credited to cash. The correcting entry is
questions.explanation: To cancel the reversed entry and record the correct one, twice the amount is needed: debit cash 36,000 and credit Femi 36,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: An accountant who refuses to inflate the profit figure despite pressure from the managing director is displaying
questions.explanation: Integrity means being straightforward and honest in all professional and business relationships, even under pressure.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: An accountant who discusses a client's tax affairs with friends at a party breaches the ethical principle of
questions.explanation: Confidentiality forbids disclosing information acquired in the course of professional work without proper authority.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: An auditor who owns a large number of shares in the company he audits lacks
questions.explanation: A financial interest in the client threatens the auditor's objectivity and independence, so it is prohibited.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The professional body whose members use the designation ACA and which was established in Nigeria in 1965 is the
questions.A: Association of National Accountants of Nigeria
questions.B: Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria
questions.C: Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria
questions.D: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria
questions.explanation: ICAN was established by Act of Parliament No. 15 of 1965 and confers the ACA and FCA designations.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The body responsible for the registration and regulation of companies in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The CAC, set up under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, registers companies and business names and keeps their statutory filings.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The Nigerian body that issues and enforces financial reporting standards for companies is the
questions.D: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria
questions.explanation: The FRCN (formerly the Nigerian Accounting Standards Board) sets and monitors compliance with accounting and auditing standards in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are issued by the
questions.explanation: The IASB, based in London, develops and publishes IFRS, which Nigeria adopted for listed companies from 2012.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The other recognised accountancy professional body in Nigeria whose members bear the designation CNA is the
questions.B: Association of National Accountants of Nigeria
questions.explanation: ANAN, established by Decree 76 of 1993, awards the Certified National Accountant (CNA) designation.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: An accountant who accepts an engagement to prepare accounts under IFRS although he has never studied the standards breaches the principle of
questions.explanation: Professional competence requires an accountant to take on only work he has the knowledge and skill to perform properly.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which quality is most essential to an accountant entrusted with public funds?
questions.explanation: Accountability means being answerable for the resources placed in one's care and being ready to give a true account of them.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The body that regulates the capital market and protects investors in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The SEC is the apex regulator of the Nigerian capital market and oversees public offers, stockbrokers and listed companies' disclosures.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The federal agency responsible for assessing and collecting companies income tax in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The FIRS administers companies income tax, petroleum profits tax and value added tax at the federal level.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Transparency in accounting means that
questions.A: profit figures are kept secret from competitors and from the tax authorities
questions.B: financial information is presented openly so that users can see how figures were arrived at
questions.C: the accountant works in an open office where every visitor can watch him
questions.D: all the figures in the accounts are rounded to the nearest million naira
questions.explanation: Transparent reporting discloses methods, assumptions and results clearly rather than hiding them.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A cashier who records fictitious payments and pockets the money is committing
questions.explanation: Fraud is a deliberate act to obtain an unjust advantage; errors are unintentional mistakes.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The main purpose of adopting IFRS in Nigeria was to
questions.A: increase the salaries and status of accountants working in Nigeria
questions.B: make Nigerian financial statements comparable with those of other countries
questions.C: reduce the number of companies registered by the Corporate Affairs Commission
questions.D: abolish the payment of companies income tax by listed companies
questions.explanation: A single set of global standards allows investors and lenders to compare companies across borders and improves confidence in Nigerian reports.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A three-column cash book has columns for
questions.explanation: The three columns on each side are discount, cash and bank; the discount columns are memorandum columns only.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The discount columns of a three-column cash book are
questions.A: balanced off at the month end exactly like the cash columns
questions.B: totalled and posted to the discount accounts in the general ledger
questions.C: ignored at the end of the month because they are memoranda
questions.D: transferred directly to the balance sheet as current assets
questions.explanation: The discount columns are memoranda: the debit-side total goes to discount allowed account and the credit-side total to discount received account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A customer who owes ₦60,000 settles his account within the discount period and is allowed 5% cash discount. The bank column and discount column entries on the debit side are
questions.explanation: Discount allowed = 5% of 60,000 = 3,000; the cheque received is 57,000, entered in the bank column, and the 3,000 in the discount allowed column.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Cash discount is given to a customer to
questions.explanation: Cash (settlement) discount is an allowance for paying within a stated period; trade discount is for bulk or trade buyers.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Discount allowed is shown in the final accounts as
questions.A: an expense in the profit and loss account
questions.B: a deduction from sales in the trading account
questions.C: an income in the profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Discount allowed to customers is a cost of collecting debts and is debited to the profit and loss account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The entry 'cash ₦50,000 paid into bank' is recorded in the cash book by
questions.A: debit bank column, credit cash column
questions.B: debit cash column, credit bank column
questions.explanation: This is a contra entry: bank receives (debit) and cash gives (credit), marked with the letter C in the folio column.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The letter 'C' written in the folio column of a cash book indicates
questions.explanation: Contra entries are transfers between the cash and bank columns; both halves are within the cash book so no ledger posting is needed.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The bank column of a cash book shows a credit balance. This means the business has
questions.explanation: A credit (excess of payments over receipts) in the bank column indicates that the business owes the bank, that is an overdraft.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The cash column of a cash book can never have a credit balance because
questions.A: cash payments are recorded on the debit side
questions.B: a business cannot pay out more cash than it has
questions.D: cash receipts are recorded in the sales day book
questions.explanation: Physical cash paid cannot exceed cash held, so the cash column always has a debit balance or nil.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader bought goods listed at ₦100,000 less 20% trade discount and paid within a week to obtain 2½% cash discount. The amount paid was
questions.explanation: Invoice price = 100,000 − 20% = 80,000; cash discount 2½% of 80,000 = 2,000; amount paid ₦78,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Discount received appears in the final accounts as
questions.A: a deduction from purchases in the trading account
questions.B: an expense in the profit and loss account
questions.C: an income in the profit and loss account
questions.D: an addition to creditors in the balance sheet
questions.explanation: Discount received from suppliers for prompt payment is a gain, credited to the profit and loss account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A business received a cheque for ₦38,000 from Ola in full settlement of a debt of ₦40,000. Two days later the cheque was dishonoured. On dishonour the correct entries are
questions.A: debit Ola ₦38,000, credit bank ₦38,000, with no entry for the discount
questions.B: debit Ola ₦40,000, credit bank ₦38,000, credit discount allowed ₦2,000
questions.C: debit bank ₦38,000, credit Ola ₦38,000, credit discount allowed ₦2,000
questions.D: debit bad debts ₦40,000, credit Ola ₦38,000, credit discount allowed ₦2,000
questions.explanation: When the cheque bounces the full debt is reinstated: the discount previously allowed is cancelled and the bank entry reversed.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In a two-column cash book, the two money columns on each side are for
questions.explanation: A two-column cash book combines the cash account and the bank account; the discount columns make it a three-column cash book.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Cash withdrawn from the bank for office use is entered in the cash book as
questions.A: debit cash column, credit bank column
questions.B: debit bank column, credit cash column
questions.explanation: Cash increases (debit cash column) and the bank balance falls (credit bank column); it is a contra entry.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The total of the discount allowed column of the cash book for a month is posted to the
questions.C: credit of each customer's account only
questions.explanation: The individual discounts are credited to the customers' accounts; the total is debited to discount allowed account to complete the double entry.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A cash book (bank column) shows receipts ₦620,000 and payments ₦655,000 for the month with an opening debit balance of ₦20,000. The closing balance is
questions.explanation: 20,000 + 620,000 − 655,000 = −15,000, that is a credit balance (overdraft) of ₦15,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: Under the imprest system, the petty cashier begins each period with
questions.B: whatever cash is left in the main cash book
questions.D: the total of last month's expenses
questions.explanation: A fixed float (imprest) is set; at the end of the period the cashier is reimbursed exactly what has been spent.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: The main advantage of the petty cash book is that it
questions.A: records all cash sales of the business
questions.B: relieves the main cash book of many small payments
questions.explanation: Numerous small payments (postage, cleaning, transport) are kept out of the main cash book and summarised through analysis columns.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: A petty cashier with an imprest of ₦20,000 spent ₦13,650 during the month and received ₦13,650 from the chief cashier. The amount in hand after reimbursement is
questions.explanation: Reimbursement restores the float to the fixed imprest amount of ₦20,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: The analysis columns of a petty cash book are used to
questions.A: classify petty expenses under headings for posting to the ledger
questions.B: record all the cash receipts of the business for the month
questions.C: calculate the discount allowed to customers who pay promptly
questions.D: list the debtors of the business and the amounts they owe
questions.explanation: Each payment is entered in the total column and again in an analysis column (e.g. postage, travelling); column totals are posted to the expense accounts.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: A payment of ₦3,000 from petty cash to a supplier, Ade, for goods bought earlier on credit is entered in the
questions.explanation: Payments to personal accounts do not fit any expense column and are analysed in the 'ledger' column for individual posting.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: The petty cashier is normally reimbursed by
questions.A: the external auditor at the end of the audit
questions.B: the chief cashier from the main cash book
questions.C: customers who pay their accounts in cash
questions.D: the bank manager on receipt of a cheque
questions.explanation: The chief cashier pays the petty cashier the amount spent, recorded as a credit in the main cash book and a debit in the petty cash book.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: A petty cash float of ₦15,000 is found to contain vouchers totalling ₦11,200 and cash of ₦3,500. The shortage is
questions.explanation: Vouchers plus cash should equal the imprest: 15,000 − (11,200 + 3,500) = ₦300 short.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: In the petty cash book, the reimbursement received from the chief cashier is entered
questions.D: on the credit side of the main cash book only
questions.explanation: Money received by the petty cashier is debited in the petty cash book; the same amount is credited in the main cash book.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: The person who signs a petty cash voucher as the recipient of money is called the
questions.explanation: The payee receives the money and signs the voucher; an authorising officer approves it.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
questions.q: A firm's imprest is ₦40,000. In June the petty cashier spent ₦28,400 and, in addition, received ₦2,000 from a staff member repaying a personal loan. The reimbursement required at the end of June is
questions.explanation: Cash in hand = 40,000 − 28,400 + 2,000 = 13,600; to restore the imprest the cashier needs 40,000 − 13,600 = ₦26,400.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared to
questions.A: find the profit of the business for the month under review
questions.B: explain the difference between the cash book balance and the bank statement balance
questions.C: record the cash sales made during the month in the cash book
questions.D: correct the errors discovered in the sales ledger and purchases ledger
questions.explanation: Timing differences and unrecorded items make the two balances differ; the statement reconciles one to the other.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A cheque issued by a business that has not yet been paid by the bank is called
questions.explanation: Unpresented (outstanding) cheques are recorded in the cash book but not yet on the bank statement.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following appears in the bank statement before it is recorded in the cash book?
questions.D: a cheque received from a customer today
questions.explanation: Bank charges are deducted by the bank and are known to the business only when the statement arrives.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Starting from a debit balance in the cash book of ₦120,000, unpresented cheques of ₦35,000 and uncredited lodgements of ₦20,000, the balance on the bank statement is
questions.explanation: Bank statement balance = 120,000 + 35,000 (bank has not yet paid them) − 20,000 (bank has not yet credited them) = ₦135,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A standing order is
questions.A: an instruction to the bank to make regular fixed payments
questions.C: a request by a creditor to collect varying amounts
questions.D: a deposit made by a customer
questions.explanation: A standing order is the customer's instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals, e.g. rent or insurance.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A direct debit differs from a standing order in that a direct debit
questions.A: is initiated by the bank without the customer's knowledge or consent
questions.B: allows the payee to collect varying amounts on the account holder's authority
questions.C: can only be used for the payment of salaries and wages to staff
questions.D: is a special form of cheque that cannot be crossed or endorsed
questions.explanation: With a direct debit the account holder authorises the payee to collect amounts which may vary, e.g. utility bills.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which item is added to the cash book balance when updating it before reconciliation?
questions.explanation: Interest or dividends received directly by the bank increase the balance and must be debited in the cash book.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A cheque received from a customer and recorded in the cash book was later returned unpaid by the bank. In the updated cash book this is
questions.C: ignored until the customer pays again
questions.explanation: The original debit for the receipt is cancelled by crediting the bank column and debiting the customer's account again.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The bank statement of a business shows an overdraft of ₦42,000. There are unpresented cheques of ₦18,000 and uncredited lodgements of ₦30,000. The cash book balance is
questions.explanation: From the bank overdraft (−42,000): deduct unpresented cheques (−18,000 → −60,000) and add uncredited lodgements (+30,000) = overdraft of ₦30,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A cheque that is presented more than six months after its date and is refused by the bank is described as
questions.explanation: Banks refuse to pay stale cheques, usually those older than six months.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A cheque dated 30 November 2026 issued on 19 September 2026 is
questions.explanation: A post-dated cheque bears a future date and cannot be paid by the bank before that date.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Two parallel lines drawn across the face of a cheque mean that the cheque
questions.A: can be cashed over the counter by anyone
questions.B: must be paid into a bank account
questions.explanation: A crossed cheque can only be paid through a bank account, which reduces the risk of loss or theft.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following bank reconciliation items is an error rather than a timing difference?
questions.A: a cheque issued last week not yet presented
questions.B: a lodgement made this morning not yet on the statement
questions.C: a cheque for ₦14,500 entered in the cash book as ₦15,400
questions.D: a standing order paid by the bank
questions.explanation: Transposition of figures is an error in the cash book; the other items arise only because of the timing of recording.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The document sent by the bank to a customer showing all transactions on the account for a period is the
questions.explanation: The bank statement is the bank's record of the customer's account and is compared with the cash book.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the bank's own books, a customer's current account balance of ₦80,000 is shown as a
questions.A: debit balance because the customer is a debtor of the bank
questions.B: credit balance because the bank owes the customer
questions.C: credit balance because it is an income of the bank
questions.D: debit balance because cash is an asset
questions.explanation: Money deposited is owed by the bank to the customer, so the bank credits the customer's account; a bank overdraft is therefore a debit in the bank's books.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader's cash book showed a bank balance of ₦64,000. The bank statement showed ₦71,300. The only differences were bank charges of ₦1,200, unpresented cheques of ₦12,000 and a lodgement not yet credited. The uncredited lodgement was
questions.explanation: Adjusted cash book = 64,000 − 1,200 = 62,800. Statement 71,300 − unpresented 12,000 + lodgement = 62,800, so the lodgement = 62,800 − 59,300 = ₦3,500.

questions.subject: Accounting

questions.explanation: Electronic banking allows credit transfers, interbank transfers and direct debits without cheques or cash.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is an instrument of bank transactions?
questions.explanation: Cheques, pay-in slips, debit and credit cards and internet transfers are instruments used to move money through a bank account.

questions.subject: Accounting

questions.explanation: Gross profit = net sales − cost of goods sold; it is the result of the trading account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Carriage inwards is debited to the trading account because it
questions.A: is a selling and distribution expense
questions.B: forms part of the cost of purchases
questions.C: reduces the sales figure of the year
questions.D: is treated as a fixed asset of the business
questions.explanation: The cost of bringing goods into the business is added to purchases; carriage outwards is a distribution expense in the profit and loss account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Which of the following is charged in the profit and loss account and not in the trading account?
questions.explanation: Carriage outwards is a selling and distribution expense; the others are trading account items.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: The goods a trader takes for his own use are
questions.A: debited to purchases and credited to drawings
questions.B: debited to drawings and credited to purchases
questions.C: debited to sales and credited to drawings
questions.explanation: Goods withdrawn reduce purchases (credit) at cost and are charged to the owner as drawings (debit).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Which of the following is a current asset?
questions.explanation: Current assets are cash or items expected to turn into cash within a year: stock, debtors, prepayments, bank and cash.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Working capital is calculated as
questions.explanation: Working capital (net current assets) measures the funds available for day-to-day operations.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Debtors ₦80,000, stock ₦120,000, bank ₦30,000, creditors ₦90,000, bank loan repayable in 5 years ₦200,000. The working capital is
questions.explanation: Current assets 230,000 − current liabilities 90,000 = ₦140,000. The long-term loan is not a current liability.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: The balance sheet of a sole trader shows
questions.A: the profit earned during the year
questions.B: the assets, liabilities and capital at a particular date
questions.C: the cash receipts and payments for the year
questions.D: the purchases and sales of the year
questions.explanation: A balance sheet is a statement of financial position at a point in time, not a record of flows during a period.

questions.subject: Accounting

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Which of the following is a long-term liability?
questions.explanation: Long-term liabilities fall due after more than one year; the others are current liabilities.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Returns inwards are deducted from
questions.explanation: Goods returned by customers reduce the sales figure, giving net sales (turnover).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Capital expenditure differs from revenue expenditure in that capital expenditure
questions.A: is charged in full to the profit and loss account of the year
questions.B: brings benefits over more than one accounting period
questions.D: relates only to goods for resale
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure acquires or improves fixed assets whose benefits last several years; revenue expenditure benefits the current period only.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Which of the following is capital expenditure?
questions.C: legal fees on the purchase of land
questions.explanation: Costs incurred in acquiring a fixed asset, including legal fees, are added to the cost of the asset.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Which of the following is revenue expenditure?
questions.A: installation cost of a new machine
questions.C: annual servicing of a delivery van
questions.explanation: Servicing maintains the asset in working order without increasing its capacity or life, so it is a revenue expense.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Which of the following is a capital receipt for a sole trader?
questions.A: cash sales of goods made during the year
questions.C: proceeds from the sale of an old delivery van
questions.D: rent received from a tenant of the business
questions.explanation: Money from disposing of a fixed asset is a capital receipt; income from normal operations is a revenue receipt.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: In the balance sheet of a sole trader, drawings are
questions.explanation: Drawings reduce the owner's investment: closing capital = opening capital + profit − drawings.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Cost of goods sold ₦480,000; opening stock ₦50,000; closing stock ₦70,000. The rate of stock turnover is
questions.explanation: Average stock = (50,000 + 70,000) ÷ 2 = 60,000; turnover = 480,000 ÷ 60,000 = 8 times a year.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Which of the following is an intangible asset?
questions.explanation: Goodwill, patents and trademarks have no physical form but have value to the business.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.q: Marshalling assets in the balance sheet in the order of permanence means
questions.A: listing cash first and land last
questions.B: listing land and buildings first and cash last
questions.explanation: In order of permanence the least liquid assets (land, buildings) come first; in order of liquidity cash comes first.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
