questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Rent of ₦120,000 per year is payable quarterly in advance. By the year end only ₦90,000 had been paid. The amount charged to the profit and loss account is
questions.explanation: The full year's rent of ₦120,000 is the expense for the period; the unpaid ₦30,000 is an accrual shown as a current liability.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: An accrued expense at the year end is shown in the balance sheet as a
questions.explanation: Expenses incurred but unpaid are owed by the business at the balance sheet date.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Insurance of ₦48,000 was paid on 1 October 2025 for the year to 30 September 2026. In the accounts to 31 December 2025 the prepaid insurance is
questions.explanation: Only 3 months (Oct–Dec) belong to 2025: 48,000 × 3/12 = 12,000 expense; the remaining 9 months, ₦36,000, is a prepayment (current asset).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A prepaid expense is treated in the balance sheet as a
questions.explanation: A prepayment is a benefit already paid for but not yet received, so it is an asset.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Rent receivable for the year is ₦200,000; only ₦170,000 was received. In the balance sheet the ₦30,000 outstanding is
questions.A: an accrued income shown as a current asset
questions.B: an accrued expense shown as a current liability
questions.explanation: Income earned but not yet received is a debtor of the business (accrued income).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A tenant paid ₦60,000 rent in December 2025 for January 2026. In the landlord's accounts for 2025 this amount is
questions.A: credited to the profit and loss account as rent income
questions.B: shown as income received in advance, a current liability
questions.explanation: The landlord has received money for a service not yet provided; it is a liability until the period it relates to.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A debt that is definitely irrecoverable because the customer has died without assets is
questions.A: written off as a bad debt
questions.B: kept in debtors until further notice
questions.C: provided for as a doubtful debt
questions.explanation: Bad debts written off are debited to bad debts account and credited to the debtor's personal account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Debtors at the year end were ₦400,000 and a provision for doubtful debts of 5% is to be maintained. The existing provision was ₦15,000. The charge to the profit and loss account is
questions.explanation: Required provision = 5% of 400,000 = 20,000; only the increase of 20,000 − 15,000 = ₦5,000 is charged this year.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Debtors ₦250,000 after writing off bad debts of ₦10,000. The provision for doubtful debts is to be reduced from ₦18,000 to 4% of debtors. The effect on the profit and loss account is
questions.explanation: New provision = 4% of 250,000 = 10,000; decrease of 18,000 − 10,000 = 8,000 is credited to profit and loss as a gain.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A provision for doubtful debts is shown in the balance sheet as
questions.explanation: Debtors are shown at cost less the provision, giving the amount expected to be collected.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A debt of ₦9,000 written off last year was recovered this year. The entry on recovery is
questions.A: debit bank, credit bad debts recovered
questions.D: debit bad debts recovered, credit bank
questions.explanation: The recovery is a gain credited to bad debts recovered account (or to bad debts account) and closed to profit and loss.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Wages for the last week of December 2025, ₦35,000, were paid on 3 January 2026. In preparing the accounts to 31 December 2025 the ₦35,000 is
questions.A: ignored because it was paid in 2026
questions.B: added to wages for 2025 and shown as an accrual
questions.explanation: Under the accrual concept the cost belongs to 2025 when the work was done.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Electricity paid during 2025 was ₦95,000. There was an accrual of ₦8,000 at the start of the year and ₦11,000 at the end. The electricity expense for 2025 is
questions.explanation: Expense = cash paid 95,000 − opening accrual 8,000 + closing accrual 11,000 = ₦98,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Rates paid in 2025 totalled ₦60,000. Rates prepaid at 1 January 2025 were ₦5,000 and at 31 December 2025 ₦9,000. The rates charged to the 2025 profit and loss account is
questions.explanation: Expense = paid 60,000 + opening prepayment 5,000 − closing prepayment 9,000 = ₦56,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The purpose of making adjustments for accruals and prepayments at the year end is to
questions.A: increase the cash balance of the business
questions.B: match expenses with the period to which they relate
questions.C: reduce the amount of tax payable on the profit
questions.D: make the two sides of the trial balance agree
questions.explanation: Adjustments apply the accrual (matching) concept so that profit reflects the period's true expenses and incomes.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A provision differs from a reserve in that a provision is
questions.A: an appropriation of profit made after the net profit has been found
questions.B: a charge against profit for a known liability or loss of uncertain amount
questions.C: always shown as a fixed asset in the balance sheet of the business
questions.D: created only by limited companies and never by sole traders
questions.explanation: Provisions (for depreciation, doubtful debts) are charges in arriving at profit; reserves are set aside out of profit already earned.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Commission received in advance at the year end is shown in the balance sheet as
questions.explanation: Income received before it is earned is owed back (in service) to the payer and is a liability at the balance sheet date.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Stock at the year end cost ₦85,000 but part of it, costing ₦15,000, is damaged and can be sold for only ₦9,000 after repairs costing ₦1,000. The closing stock value is
questions.explanation: Damaged goods are valued at net realisable value 9,000 − 1,000 = 8,000 instead of cost 15,000; total = 70,000 + 8,000 = ₦78,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Depreciation is best described as the
questions.A: cash set aside each year in a special fund to replace a fixed asset
questions.B: fall in the market price of an asset between two balance sheet dates
questions.C: systematic allocation of the cost of a fixed asset over its useful life
questions.D: loss made when a fixed asset is sold for less than its original cost
questions.explanation: Depreciation spreads the cost of a fixed asset over the periods that benefit from it, in line with the matching concept.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Which of the following is not a cause of depreciation?
questions.explanation: Depreciation arises from use, time, obsolescence and depletion; a rise in market value is the opposite of depreciation.

questions.subject: Accounting

questions.q: A van costing ₦1,500,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum by the reducing-balance method. The depreciation for the second year is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Under the reducing-balance method the depreciation charge
questions.D: is charged only in the year of purchase
questions.explanation: A fixed percentage is applied to a falling net book value, so the annual charge falls year by year.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: The method of depreciation most suitable for a quarry or an oil well is the
questions.explanation: Wasting assets are depreciated according to the quantity extracted in each period.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Net book value of a fixed asset is
questions.explanation: Net book value (written-down value) is the amount at which an asset is carried in the balance sheet.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: An asset bought for ₦640,000 is depreciated at 25% per annum on the reducing balance. Its net book value after two years is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: The double entry for the annual depreciation charge is
questions.A: debit provision for depreciation, credit profit and loss
questions.B: debit profit and loss (depreciation expense), credit provision for depreciation
questions.C: debit fixed asset, credit provision for depreciation
questions.explanation: The expense is charged to profit and loss and accumulated in the provision (accumulated depreciation) account, leaving the asset at cost.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Loose tools are usually depreciated by the
questions.explanation: Small tools are revalued at the year end; the fall in value (plus purchases, less opening value) is the depreciation.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: A machine costing ₦900,000 has a life of 4 years and no scrap value. Using the sum-of-the-years'-digits method, the depreciation for the first year is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: An asset with a net book value of ₦150,000 is sold for ₦180,000. The disposal results in
questions.explanation: Proceeds exceed the net book value by 180,000 − 150,000 = ₦30,000, credited to profit and loss as a profit on disposal.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: When a fixed asset is sold, the accumulated depreciation on it is transferred to the
questions.C: credit of the profit and loss account
questions.explanation: The disposal account is debited with cost and credited with accumulated depreciation and sale proceeds; the balance is the profit or loss.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Land is not normally depreciated because it
questions.explanation: Land does not wear out or become obsolete, so its cost is not allocated over time (buildings on it are depreciated).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: A machine bought on 1 July 2024 for ₦1,200,000 is depreciated at 10% per annum on cost, time-apportioned. The financial year ends on 31 December. The accumulated depreciation at 31 December 2025 is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: A provision for depreciation account is
questions.A: a real account with a debit balance
questions.B: a nominal account closed to trading account
questions.C: a credit balance representing depreciation charged to date
questions.explanation: It accumulates the depreciation charged since purchase and is deducted from the asset's cost in the balance sheet.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Which method charges more depreciation in the early years of an asset's life?
questions.explanation: Reducing balance front-loads the charge, which is appropriate when repairs rise as the asset ages, keeping total annual cost fairly even.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: A trader sold a van for ₦350,000. It had cost ₦1,000,000 and accumulated depreciation to the date of sale was ₦600,000. The profit or loss on disposal was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: The cost of a fixed asset for depreciation purposes includes
questions.B: the cost of installing the asset
questions.explanation: All costs of bringing the asset to working condition (carriage, installation, legal fees) are capitalised; running costs are expenses.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Depreciation and Disposal of Fixed Assets
questions.q: Which of the following is depreciated by the depletion method?
questions.explanation: Natural resources such as timber, mines and quarries are written off according to the quantity extracted.
